sun.title: The Sun
sun.html:
The Sun holds 99.86% of the solar system's mass. Its pull never lets go of a planet, while the planet keeps rushing forward — so it neither falls in nor flies off, but goes round and round.

The farther out, the weaker the pull, the slower the planet and the longer its path: Mercury's year is 88 days, Saturn's nearly 29 Earth years.

brief.subject: How the solar system moves
brief.intent: Why the planets go round the Sun, and why the farther out a planet is, the longer its year
brief.concept: Seen from above the North Pole: the Sun in the middle, six orbits nested one inside the next, each planet moving at its true pace, slower the farther out — a child sees 'farther is slower' without reading a word. Earth opens onto its water cycle, and a tree there onto one leaf.
brief.direction: Crayon: thick black strokes, saturated flat fills with grain, big friendly handwriting
